title: Pay real estate and personal property taxes
question: How and when do I pay my Albemarle County property tax bill?
office: Department of Finance & Budget, Office of Revenue Administration (payments); the Director of Finance performs the treasurer's duties under the county executive form
summary: Albemarle has no elected treasurer: the Department of Finance & Budget's Office of Revenue Administration bills and collects real estate and personal property (vehicle) taxes. Both are due in halves on June 25 and December 5, or the next business day if the date falls on a weekend; the June bill includes the vehicle license fee. Pay online at albemarlecountytaxes.org (e-check free, cards 2.35% to 2.5%), by phone at 866-820-5450, by mail to P.O. Box 7604, Merrifield, VA 22116-7604 (postmarked by the due date), at the 24-hour kiosk or drop boxes, or in person at 401 McIntire Road. Late payment adds 10% or $10, plus 10% yearly interest. If you fall behind, call 434-296-5851.

steps.step: Note the two due dates: June 25 and December 5 each year
steps.who: Taxpayer (for real estate, the owner on January 1); the Department of Finance & Budget bills and collects
steps.how: Real estate tax and personal property tax (cars, trucks, motorcycles, boats, trailers, mobile homes) are each billed in two halves. The first half is due June 25 and the second half December 5. If a due date falls on a weekend, it moves to the next business day. Real estate bills go out by post each spring and fall to the owner. The yearly vehicle license fee is added to the June 25 personal property bill. Business tangible personal property, machinery and tools, and public service property have the same dates.
steps.deadline: June 25 and December 5 (next business day if the date falls on a weekend)
steps.fee: Calendar year 2026 rates: real estate $0.894 per $100 of assessed value; personal property $4.28 per $100 of assessed value

steps.step: Receive the bill, and ask for it if it has not arrived before the due date
steps.who: Department of Finance & Budget, Office of Revenue Administration (sends bills); taxpayer
steps.how: State law requires bills to be mailed at least 14 days before the due date. The county may choose not to mail a bill of $20 or less. The county's penalty policy says that not receiving a bill, or a bill sent to the wrong address, is not a reason to waive the penalty. If you have no bill shortly before the due date, look it up in the online payment portal or call the Office of Revenue Administration at 434-296-5851 and pay on time.
steps.deadline: Bills are to be mailed no later than 14 days before the due date (Va. Code § 58.1-3912(A))
steps.quote: If no bill is received that duty includes contacting the taxing authority prior to the due date and paying on time

steps.who: Taxpayer; the county's e-statement portal (run by a vendor)
steps.how: Go to Albemarle.estmt.net and choose Create an Account. Enter the Registration ID printed on your bill and your name exactly as it appears on the bill. Each parcel has its own Registration ID, and you can link more bills after you set up the account. Future bills then arrive as an email from documents@albemarle.estmt.net. The county page lists the vendor's support desk for help with enrolment: 1-800-549-4722, Monday to Friday, 8 am to 5 pm Eastern.

steps.step: Check the bill, and fix errors with the office that assessed the tax
steps.who: Taxpayer; Office of Revenue Administration, Business & Personal Tax Unit (vehicles and other personal property); County Assessor's Office (real estate values and mailing addresses for real estate)
steps.how: Check each vehicle and whether it got car tax relief (PPTR); relief is applied automatically to qualifying vehicles. If you sold, traded or junked a vehicle, tell Virginia DMV first and then the county; assessments and refunds depend on the date DMV records. If you moved to another Virginia locality, update your address, garage jurisdiction and move date with DMV and contact the county. If you moved to another state, register the vehicle there and send the county a copy of the new state's registration showing the date it was registered (or, if you sold it before registering it there, the bill of sale), within 30 days of the move; the county keeps taxing the vehicle until it has that evidence. Questions on vehicles go to 434-296-5852 or tax@albemarle.org. Questions on a real estate value go to the County Assessor's Office at 434-296-5856. To change the mailing address for real estate bills, use the Assessor's Address Change form.

steps.step: If a mortgage company pays your real estate tax from escrow, check that it has paid
steps.who: Property owner; mortgage company or servicer
steps.how: Mortgage companies and servicers can get tax due information through a third-party service or by sending the county a list of parcels in its Claim File Layout, and they pay electronically in the county's Payment File Layout. The files go to the Office of Revenue Administration. If the lender does not pay, state law has the past-due bill sent to you, and penalty and interest apply to any unpaid tax. Check the parcel's balance in the online portal before each due date.

steps.who: Taxpayer; Office of Revenue Administration (through the county's separate payment website)
steps.how: From the Pay Taxes page, choose Pay Personal Property and Real Estate Taxes, which opens the county's separate payment website. Pay by electronic check from a checking account (free), or by Visa, Mastercard, Discover or American Express credit or debit card, or PayPal. You do not need a PayPal account. Partial payments are accepted, but they are applied to the oldest balance first and do not stop penalty and interest on the unpaid part. Business taxes are paid through a separate business tax portal.
steps.fee: E-check: no fee. Card payments (processed by PayPal): credit cards 2.50%, debit cards 2.35%, minimum $1.95

steps.how: Call 866-820-5450 to pay real estate or personal property tax by card or electronic check.
steps.fee: As printed in the phone section: debit cards 2.50%, credit cards 2.35%, minimum $1.95; electronic checks no fee
steps.quote: To Pay Real Estate/Personal Property taxes call 866-820-5450.

steps.who: Taxpayer; the county's mail payment processor (Direct Mail Processors)
steps.how: Follow the payment instructions attached to your bill: make the check payable to County of Albemarle and mail it to County of Albemarle, P.O Box 7604, Merrifield VA 22116-7604. A third-party vendor processes mailed payments for the county. The county warns that the post office may cause delays, so mail early.
steps.deadline: Postmarked on or before the due date

steps.how: The automated kiosk is at the County Office Building, 401 McIntire Road, on the side facing Preston Avenue. It takes cash, checks and credit cards, gives change in bills (no coins), and applies any overpayment to future bills.

steps.step: Or leave a check in a county drop box
steps.how: Drop boxes are at the County Office Building, 401 McIntire Road (in the parking lot by the Visitor's Entrance and in the lower commuter parking lot), and at the 5th Street County Office Building, 1600 5th Street. The 5th Street box is open only from June 1 to June 25 and from November 1 to December 5. Do not put cash in a drop box.
steps.deadline: By the due date; the 5th Street box is open only June 1 to June 25 and November 1 to December 5 (or the next business day if the due date falls on a holiday or weekend)

steps.step: Or pay in person at the County Office Building
steps.how: Go to the Office of Revenue Administration on the 1st floor of the County Office Building, 401 McIntire Road, Charlottesville, Monday to Friday, 8:00 am to 5:00 pm, except holidays. You can pay by cash, check, credit or debit card, or money order. State law entitles you to a receipt on request.
steps.fee: Card payments: credit cards 2.50%, debit cards 2.35%, minimum $1.95

steps.step: Pay any supplemental bill by its own due date
steps.how: A supplemental bill adjusts a current or earlier year's bill, or taxes property newly found in the county, for example a vehicle bought after the regular bills went out, a vehicle wrongly garaged elsewhere, a reactivated tag, a business-use vehicle that lost car tax relief, or a new or improved home valued after January 1. It can cover up to three prior years and the current year. These bills are mailed two or three times a year and have their own due dates. Questions go to payments@albemarle.org or 434-296-5851.
steps.deadline: The date printed on the supplemental bill (the 2021 proposed amendment to County Code § 15-101, agenda item 21-461, would set it at 45 days from the bill date; its adoption was not confirmed)

steps.step: If you pay late: a penalty of 10% or $10, then 10% a year interest
steps.how: The penalty is charged the day after the due date and becomes part of the tax. It is 10 percent (at least $10) of the unpaid balance of each assessed item, but never more than the tax. Interest of 10% a year runs on the unpaid tax and penalty from the first day of the month after the due date until paid. A delinquent notice showing the penalty is mailed 14 days after each deadline.
steps.deadline: Penalty the day after the due date; interest from the first day of the following month
steps.fee: Penalty 10% or $10, whichever is greater (not more than the tax); interest 10% a year

steps.step: Ask the county to waive a penalty that was not your fault
steps.who: Taxpayer to the Department of Finance & Budget, Office of Revenue Administration (the Director of Finance performs the treasurer's role)
steps.how: The county's penalty policy allows a waiver if the payment was late because of a medically determinable physical or mental impairment and was paid within 30 days of the due date; if the underlying tax is abated, or the tax was not assessed on time because of a clerical error by the assessing staff; if the lateness was solely the county's fault; or if the Postmaster admits in writing that the Post Office caused a late postmark. State law also excuses a payment shown to be on time by a USPS Certificate of Mailing or other proof of mailing, and treats the taxpayer's death, like a medical impairment, as presumptive proof of no fault if the tax is paid within 30 days of the due date (within 120 days after a fiduciary qualifies, where one handles the taxpayer's affairs); interest still accrues until paid. The policy refuses a waiver for not knowing the deadline, not receiving a bill, a bill sent to the wrong address, an incorrect bill, or wrong information from county staff. No request form or written procedure is published; contact the Office of Revenue Administration with your documents.
steps.deadline: None stated for the request; for the medical-impairment ground, the tax must have been paid within 30 days of the due date

steps.step: If you are deployed outside the United States with the armed forces: automatic extension
steps.who: Service member; Department of Finance & Budget
steps.how: State law requires an automatic extension for members of the U.S. armed services deployed outside the United States, including active duty in the regular forces, the National Guard and the reserves. It covers real estate tax on a primary residence and personal property tax on a qualifying vehicle. The taxes fall due 90 days after the deployment ends. The county pages read do not say how to tell the county, so call the Office of Revenue Administration. A separate exemption for service members whose home of record is not Virginia is handled by the Business & Personal Tax Unit.
steps.quote: Such extension shall end and the taxes shall be due 90 days following the completion of such member's deployment.

steps.step: If you cannot pay in full, call the Office of Revenue Administration early
steps.who: Taxpayer; Office of Revenue Administration (delinquent collections)
steps.how: Call 434-296-5851 as soon as possible. The county says this helps keep penalty and interest down and avoid the extra fee charged when an account is sent to the collection agency. The county pages do not describe an installment plan for current taxes, and no third-party tax payment agreement program was found.
steps.quote: If you by chance become delinquent, please do not hesitate to contact the Revenue Administration at 434-296-5851 as soon as possible

steps.step: If taxes stay unpaid: DMV hold, liens, refund set-off and a collection agency
steps.who: Department of Finance & Budget, Office of Revenue Administration; Virginia DMV; Virginia Department of Taxation; the county's collection agency (Taxing Authority Consulting Services, PC)
steps.how: After the delinquent notice, the county can block DMV registration renewal for every vehicle you own or co-own until all delinquent taxes are paid; allow 2 business days after paying for the hold to clear. State law requires notice of the intended refusal at least 30 days before the current registration expires. It can issue tax liens, without going to court, on salary, bank accounts, rent owed by a tenant, unclaimed property and, for businesses, amounts owed by a credit card company. A lien on wages or salary is generally limited by state law to 25% of disposable earnings each pay period. Each November 1 it sends delinquent accounts to the Department of Taxation, which can take the debt from a state income tax refund or lottery winnings. Accounts 3 months or more delinquent can go to a private collection agency, which adds 20%. The county may also sue and obtain a judgment.
steps.deadline: Delinquent notice 14 days after each deadline; set-off list sent each November 1; collection agency after 3 months or more of delinquency; a treasurer's lien is allowed once taxes are more than 30 days delinquent (Va. Code § 58.1-3952(B))
steps.fee: DMV hold removal $25; refund set-off $25 county fee plus 4% of the amount withheld (Department of Taxation); collection agency 20% of the amount collected

steps.step: If real estate tax stays unpaid: judicial sale, and the right to redeem
steps.who: Department of Finance & Budget (through its tax sale firm, Taxing Authority Consulting Services, P.C.); Albemarle County Circuit Court
steps.how: A parcel can be sold at a judicial sale once its taxes are still unpaid on December 31 after the second anniversary of the due date. State law allows sale after the first anniversary for parcels with a condemned structure, a nuisance, a derelict building or a blighted property, and, on a court finding, for parcels assessed at $100,000 or less. The process can take about 18 months. The owner can redeem the property at any time before the sale by paying all taxes, penalties, interest, attorney's fees and costs. State law requires a notice at least 30 days before the suit is filed, telling the owner that a payment agreement of up to 72 months can be requested; such an agreement can suspend the sale.
steps.deadline: Eligible for sale when delinquent on December 31 following the second anniversary of the due date; redemption before the sale date
steps.fee: All taxes, penalties and interest plus costs, including publication costs and a reasonable attorney fee set by the court

fees.quote: The administrative costs shall be in addition to all penalties and interest, and shall not exceed $30 for taxes or other charges collected subsequent to 30 or more days after notice of delinquent taxes or charges pursuant to § 58.1-3919 but prior to the taking of any judgment with respect to such delinquent taxes or charges, and $35 for taxes or other charges collected subsequent to judgment.

fees.item: Returned (dishonored) check or payment
fees.amount: $35 or the amount of any costs, whichever is greater (state law; the county pages do not state a returned-payment fee)
fees.quote: A penalty of $35 or the amount of any costs, whichever is greater, shall be added to such amount.

fees.item: Additional paper receipt
fees.amount: Up to $2 (state cap; county practice not stated)
fees.quote: charge a reasonable sum, not to exceed two dollars, to cover the cost of preparing any additional receipt.

fees.item: Redeeming real estate before a judicial sale
fees.amount: All taxes, penalties and interest, plus costs including publication and a reasonable attorney fee set by the court
fees.quote: together with all costs including costs of publication and a reasonable attorney fee set by the court.

escalation.trigger: A late penalty or interest was charged and the lateness was not your fault (medical impairment, county error, Post Office error, proof of timely mailing)
escalation.next: Department of Finance & Budget, Office of Revenue Administration: ask for a waiver (the Director of Finance makes the fault decision in the treasurer's role)
escalation.deadline: None stated for the request; for the medical-impairment ground, the tax must have been paid within 30 days of the due date
escalation.quote: The treasurer shall make determinations of fault relating exclusively to failure to pay a tax

escalation.trigger: You cannot pay on time or have fallen behind
escalation.next: Office of Revenue Administration (delinquent collections), 434-296-5851; no published installment plan for current taxes
escalation.deadline: As soon as possible; accounts go to the collection agency after 3 months or more of delinquency
escalation.quote: If you by chance become delinquent, please do not hesitate to contact the Revenue Administration at 434-296-5851 as soon as possible

escalation.trigger: You cannot pay the full amount and its collection is in substantial doubt (the collecting official decides this, and whether a compromise serves the county's interest)
escalation.next: Director of Finance (as collecting official): a written offer in compromise, which needs the consent of the Board of Supervisors or its designee (Va. Code § 58.1-3994(B))
escalation.quote: Any offer in compromise submitted to an official responsible for the assessment or collection of local taxes shall be made in writing and shall be deemed accepted only when the taxpayer is notified in writing of the acceptance by the responsible official.

escalation.trigger: The personal property (vehicle) amount on the bill is wrong: vehicle sold or moved, not taxable here, wrong car tax relief status, or a damaged vehicle valued at the clean trade-in price
escalation.next: Department of Finance & Budget, Business & Personal Tax Unit: a written request for correction of assessment, or for damage existing on January 1, the Notice of Appeal of Vehicle Personal Property Assessment (form f1) with an itemized estimate. Under Va. Code § 58.1-3916, a correction appeal filed within 90 days of the assessment keeps the bill from being treated as delinquent and sent to collection until 30 days after the decision, but the county's appeal form warns that appealing does not relieve you of paying all taxes by the bill's due date so no late-payment penalty applies, so pay on time and ask for a refund. Damage adjustments do not renew; the form must be filed each year.
escalation.deadline: Within three years from the last day of the tax year, or within one year from the date of the assessment, whichever is later; an unpaid vehicle tax can also be challenged at any time while it is collectible, with clear factual evidence that you were not subject to it (Va. Code § 58.1-3980(B))
escalation.quote: apply to the commissioner of the revenue or such other official who made the assessment for a correction thereof.

escalation.trigger: You disagree with the real estate assessment behind the bill
escalation.next: County Assessor's Office: request an Assessor's review (forms from the Assessor's Office)
escalation.deadline: By March 2, 2026 for the 2026 assessment (set each year)

escalation.trigger: You still disagree with the real estate assessment (with or without an Assessor's review)
escalation.next: Albemarle County Board of Equalization (appeal forms only from the County Assessor's Office; Va. Code § 58.1-3379)
escalation.deadline: March 30, 2026, or within 30 days of the Assessor's review letter, whichever is later

escalation.trigger: You are still aggrieved by an assessment after the county's decision, or the county has not decided (the county's Taxpayer Appeal Rights page says the taxpayer can appeal to the circuit court at any stage of the administrative review)
escalation.next: Albemarle County Circuit Court: application for relief from an erroneous assessment
escalation.deadline: Within three years from the last day of the tax year, within one year from the assessment, or within one year from a final local or Tax Commissioner determination, whichever is later
escalation.quote: apply for relief to the circuit court of the county or city wherein such assessment was made.

escalation.trigger: Your real estate is listed for a judicial sale for unpaid taxes
escalation.next: Department of Finance & Budget (through its tax sale firm): a payment agreement of up to 72 months, which can suspend the sale; or redeem by paying everything due into court before the sale date
escalation.deadline: Before the date set for the judicial sale
escalation.quote: may suspend any action for sale of the property commenced pursuant to this article (i) upon entering into an agreement with the owner of the real property for the payment of all delinquent amounts in installments over a period that is reasonable under the circumstances, but that in no event shall exceed 72 months

caveats: Albemarle County's website (www.albemarle.org) refuses automated readers, so the county pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. The Internet Archive holds no later 2026 copy of the Important Dates and Deadlines page than the one of March 8, 2026. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them before you act.

Local ordinance not read. The County Code is published only on Municode, whose terms forbid automated access, so no County Code text is quoted. The penalty (§ 15-103(A)) and interest (§ 15-104) are quoted from the county's own penalty policy page, which restates them. The due-date sections (§ 15-101 and § 15-1404) are described from the Board of Supervisors' 2021 agenda item 21-461 in the county's Legistar system, Legistar records no vote on that item, so its adoption is not confirmed there; the 2026 county pages all state June 25 and December 5. The ordinance and resolution attachments have not been checked.

Tax rates. The 2026 rates ($0.894 per $100 for real estate and $4.28 per $100 for personal property) come from the Board's April 22, 2026 agenda item 26-256 (adopted, per its Legistar history) and the Personal Property page. The Real Estate page copy of August 2026 still says "The 2025 Real Estate Tax Rate is $0.894 per hundred of assessed value", which is the same rate. A proposal to raise the personal property rate to $4.43 (item 26-240) was tabled. The 2026 car tax relief (PPTR) percentage was not found; the latest listed is 42% for 2025.

Card fees conflict on the Payment Options page. The online and in-person sections give credit cards 2.50% and debit cards 2.35%. The phone section prints the reverse (debit cards 2.50%, credit cards 2.35%), and the kiosk section gives a 2.5% credit card fee. The dates page also mentions PayPal as a payment method. Check the fee shown before paying.

The pay-by-phone number (866-820-5450) is the same number the dates page gives for the collection agency's "General Collections" line, so the phone payment line may be run by the county's contractor. This was not confirmed.
The payment portal (www.albemarlecountytaxes.org) is a JavaScript application run on a vendor platform (Catalis). Its payment screens, fee display and terms of use are not described here.

Mailbox mismatch: on the Payment Options page the visible address is payments@albemarle.org, but the link behind it points to a different collections mailbox. The visible address, which also appears on the Pay Taxes, Supplemental Bills and Real Estate pages, is recorded.

Penalty waivers. The county's policy borrows treasurer and commissioner wording (the Director of Finance performs both roles) and refers to approval "by the Treasurer". No form, address or written procedure for asking for a waiver is published. Under Va. Code § 58.1-3916 the governing body may delegate fault decisions where there is no treasurer; no delegation ordinance was found, so who decides was not confirmed beyond the policy page.

Timeliness. The county counts postmarks for mail. State law also accepts a commercial delivery service's confirmation of shipment (Va. Code § 58.1-9(A)) and a USPS Certificate of Mailing or other proof of mailing (§ 58.1-3916). For electronic payments, § 58.1-9(B) counts funds received by midnight on the due date; the county pages do not say how card or e-check payments made on the due date are dated.

Weekends and holidays. The county pages move a weekend due date to the next business day but say nothing about holidays, except the drop-box note. Va. Code § 1-210(E) also moves a deadline that falls on a legal holiday or an office-closure day to the next business day.

Payment plans. No installment plan for current taxes, no extension resolution under Va. Code § 58.1-3916 and no third-party tax payment agreement under § 58.1-3018 were found for Albemarle. The 72-month payment agreement in § 58.1-3965 applies once a judicial sale is being prepared. The county does accept deposits toward next year's personal property tax (Personal Property FAQ).

Supplemental bills. The Supplemental Bills page does not state how many days these bills allow. The 45-day period comes from the 2021 proposed ordinance (item 21-461); its adoption was not confirmed in Legistar. State law (Va. Code § 58.1-3903) starts penalty and interest only 30 days after the assessment when an omitted assessment was not the taxpayer's fault.

Real estate appeals are summarised only as escalation. The dates given (March 2 and March 30, 2026) are for the 2026 assessment and change each year. The Real Estate page says both that an appeal form "must be postmarked or received" by the deadline and that mailed appeals "must be received by our office, regardless of the postmark date"; deliver it early. Board of Equalization appeal forms are available only from the County Assessor's Office.

Bills must be mailed at least 14 days before the due date (Va. Code § 58.1-3912(A)). The 30-day rule in § 58.1-3912(C) applies only to counties next to an urban county executive county; on that reading it does not apply to Albemarle, but this was not confirmed.

The collection fees (the $25 DMV stop fee, the $25 set-off fee plus 4%, and the 20% collection agency fee) are as stated on the county page. The county pages do not mention the $30 and $35 administrative costs allowed by Va. Code § 58.1-3958, or any returned-check fee.

Not covered: business tangible personal property, machinery and tools, and other business taxes, which are filed and paid through the separate business tax portal; real estate tax relief for the elderly and disabled; the disabled veteran exemptions; land use deferral; and taxes of the Town of Scottsville. Many Albemarle addresses have a Charlottesville mailing address. Property inside the City of Charlottesville is taxed by the City Treasurer, not the county.

Escrowed real estate: the county page describes mortgage-company files and payments. It does not say whether the owner also gets a copy of the bill. The statement that penalty and interest still apply if a lender does not pay rests on state law (Va. Code §§ 58.1-3912(A), 58.1-3916), not a county page.

Staff names, and the personal mailboxes and booking links on some county pages, are deliberately not recorded. Only office lines, office mailboxes (payments@, tax@, CountyAssessor@), the office addresses and the portals are kept.

Appeals and late penalty. Va. Code § 58.1-3916 says a bill under a timely administrative appeal is not deemed delinquent and subject to collection during the appeal, while the county's vehicle appeal form says an appeal does not relieve the taxpayer of paying by the due date so no late-payment penalty applies. How the county reconciles the two was not found; paying on time and seeking a refund avoids the question.

The 2026 rate quote ($0.894 and $4.28) is from the staff report of agenda item 26-256, which describes Attachment A; the resolution itself is an attachment on albemarle.legistar1.com and was not read. Legistar's history records the Board's adoption of the tax-rate resolution on April 22, 2026, and the county's Tax Rates and Personal Property pages give the same rates.

Form of government. The county's penalty policy says only that Albemarle "has adopted an alternate form of government" without a Commissioner of the Revenue or Treasurer. This page reads that as the county executive form, whose director of finance collects taxes and has a treasurer's powers (Va. Code §§ 15.2-519, 15.2-522); no county page cited here names the form, so that reading is not confirmed from a county source. The collecting office itself is confirmed by the county pages.

corrections: legal_basis (items 21-461): the three due-date entries are now cited as a proposed amendment to County Code §§ 15-101 and 15-1404, quoted from the agenda item's title, with no vote recorded in Legistar (the Legistar matter, its histories and the October 6, 2021 event items were re-read; the item shows no action).

legal_basis and fees (item 26-256): the rate quote is from the staff report describing Attachment A, not from the resolution's own text; the citation now says so. Legistar's history records the resolution's adoption on April 22, 2026.

s4: the vehicle-move guidance said to update DMV first for every move. The Moving and Personal Property pages say an out-of-state mover registers the vehicle in the new state and sends the county the new registration showing its date (or a bill of sale) within 30 days, and that the vehicle stays taxable until the county has it; an in-state mover updates address, garage jurisdiction and move date with DMV. Reworded.
s8: the county says the check-payment instructions are attached to the bill; the step had the taxpayer mailing the instructions with the check. Reworded.

s14: the policy's clerical-error ground is that the tax was not assessed on time because of a clerical error by the assessing staff, not that it was 'billed late'; added the state-law death ground and the 120-day fiduciary rule from Va. Code § 58.1-3916, with a new legal_basis entry.

s17: added the 30-day notice before a DMV registration refusal (Va. Code § 46.2-752(J)) and the general 25% limit on wage and salary liens (Va. Code § 58.1-3952(B), as amended in 2026), with legal_basis entries.

s18: added the earlier, first-anniversary sale routes in Va. Code § 58.1-3965(A) (condemned, nuisance, derelict or blighted property; parcels assessed at $100,000 or less on a court finding), with a legal_basis entry.
Fee 'State cap on the late payment penalty': the 25% cap applies to tangible personal property tax more than 30 days past due, not to 'some personal property'; added that the county pages state 10%.
Escalation rung 3 (offer in compromise): removed '(for example, serious hardship)', which neither § 58.1-3994 nor a county page says; the trigger now follows § 58.1-3994(B).

Escalation rung 4 (vehicle correction): added the county appeal form's warning that an appeal does not relieve the taxpayer of paying by the due date to avoid a late penalty, that damage adjustments must be refiled each year, and the any-time challenge to an unpaid vehicle tax with clear factual evidence (Va. Code § 58.1-3980(B)); two legal_basis entries added and a caveat on the § 58.1-3916 appeal rule.

Escalation rung 7 (Circuit Court): the parenthetical that the court does not require the administrative steps first was not in § 58.1-3984; it now rests on the county Taxpayer Appeal Rights page, quoted in a new local legal_basis entry.

Added caveats on the verification re-read, the appeal and penalty interplay, the 26-256 staff report, and the unconfirmed form-of-government reading; added the Legistar 26-240 matter and the October 6, 2021 event items to sources.
open_issues: www.albemarle.org refuses automated requests (HTTP 403, robots.txt included); every county page and PDF was checked against Internet Archive copies dated March to September 2026, not the live site, so later changes would be missed.

County Code (Municode) not read under its terms; the penalty (§ 15-103(A)) and interest (§ 15-104) rest on the county's restatement, and the adoption of the 2021 due-date amendment (item 21-461) is not recorded in Legistar. The county pages consistently state June 25 and December 5.
The Payment Options page prints the phone-payment card fees the other way round from the online and in-person sections; the file reports both as printed.

No published waiver request form, installment plan for current taxes, or third-party tax payment agreement; the 2026 car tax relief percentage was not found; the payment portal's own fee display and terms were not read.
Whether Albemarle's form of government is the county executive form (Va. Code §§ 15.2-519, 15.2-522) was not confirmed from a county source read in the check.
